subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests tolerate or ignore a generic request-body `model`, instead of validating that body field as an OpenClaw agent target?
rationale: The code change is mechanically narrow, but it changes a documented public Gateway API contract and should be consistent across sibling OpenAI-compatible HTTP surfaces.

options.title: Decide shared endpoint semantics first
options.body: Keep this issue open until Gateway owners choose one precedence rule for chat completions, responses, and embeddings before implementation.

options.title: Adopt header precedence
options.body: Treat generic body `model` values as compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, then update shared resolver behavior, docs, and tests.

options.title: Preserve agent-first contract
options.body: Continue requiring body `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or an agent-target value, and document SDK integrations around those values plus `x-openclaw-model`.

recommendation.title: Decide shared endpoint semantics first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until Gateway owners choose one precedence rule for chat completions, responses, and embeddings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current agent-first contract and sibling endpoint expansion trace most directly to vincentkoc's Gateway history.
